finding: Cross-substrate cascade-match test against the strongest decentralised-substrate candidate available: cephalopod nervous system. ~500M neurons total, ~2/3 distributed across 8 anatomically autonomous arm-ganglia, confirmed cyclic-ring inter-arm topology, segmental ANC repeat structure, distributed chromatophore + papillae motoneuron pools in peripheral stellate ganglion. End-goal candidate: integrated embodied cognition without centralised processor. Hypothesised class chain: L (distributed-neuron Laplacian per arm + central) ∘ C (sensorimotor cascade-orientation) ∘ M (cross-arm HDC binding) ∘ I (8-arm cyclic-group ring + per-sucker ℤ/n).

finding: CLASS-L-INSTANTIATED-IN-MULTIPLE-SUBSTRATES. Per-arm ANC neural graph Laplacian: ~40M neurons each, dominated by short-range ipsilateral + mid-range adjacent-sucker projections (Olson et al. 2025 PMC11736069). Central-brain Laplacian: vertical lobe + optic lobes + connecting tracts described as 'richly interconnected and reentrant' (Ponte et al. 2022 PMC9039538). Chromatophore Turing-CA model explicitly identifies convolution-equivalent Laplacian: N1, N2 neighbourhood-sum filters acting as 'convolution operation equivalent to' Laplacian on local chromatophore grid (Ishida 2021 PMC8357167). Class L is instantiated at THREE distinct partition-coexistent substrates within the same animal: per-arm ANC + central-brain + epidermis chromatophore grid.

finding: CLASS-C-INSTANTIATED-IN-MOTOR-PRIMITIVE-COMPOSITION. Levy & Hochner 2017 PMC5368235 explicitly identifies motor primitives as composable building blocks: 'stereotypical movement combination of several motor primitives' (bend / elongate / shorten / torsion) reducing reach to '3 or 4 DOF'. Zullo et al. 2019 PMC6478645 documents 'en passant' synaptic recruitment: descending motor axons synapse simultaneously to large motor neuron pools without somatotopic specificity — direct cascade-dispatch via Class C ∘ Class D composition. Embodied integration model: central command + local sensory → integrated peripheral motor output, all expressible in framework Class C.

finding: CLASS-M-INSTANTIATED-IN-CROSS-ARM-BINDING. Carls-Diamante 2022 PMC8988249 explicitly invokes binding language: 'whether the octopus experiences one single unified field or multiple distinct ones depends on how well they are bound together.' Intact octopus achieves unified-behaviour despite 8 anatomically autonomous arm-ganglia → some binding operation must occur. Candidate cephalopod substrate: cerebrobrachial tract + nerve-ring intersection (sparse ~32,000 efferents + 30,000 inter-region fibres per Zullo et al. 2019 + Carls-Diamante 2022). Framework primitive srmech.amsc.bind (Class M HDC XOR self-inverse shipped 0.4.0rcN) is the cleanest formal expression of the operation cephalopod biology requires.
anchor_citation: Carls-Diamante 2022 PMC8988249; Zullo et al. 2019 PMC6478645

finding: CLASS-I-LITERALLY-INSTANTIATED-IN-NERVE-RING. Strongest single anatomical-cascade match in the spike. Chang & Hale 2023 PMC10192654 documents the inter-arm nerve ring as 'a set of interbrachial commissures that bridge between the axial nerve cords of neighboring arms to form a continuous morphological neural connection around all eight.' Explicit language: 'interbrachial connections are in the form of a ring.' Eight-fold radial symmetry produces literal ℤ/8ℤ cyclic-group topology in neural hardware. Sucker segmentation: Olson et al. 2025 PMC11736069 reports ~7.5 segments per sucker (range 7.64-7.88) as ℤ/n cyclic-cascade structure within each arm. Class I (cyclic-group / modular arithmetic, shipped srmech.amsc.cyclic 0.4.0rc1) is the precise formal model for the anatomical topology.
anchor_class: I (cyclic group ℤ/8ℤ on ring; ℤ/n on segments)

finding: PARTITION-COEXISTENT-INSTANTIATION. Per [[user_stance_substrate_identity_partition_coexistence_canonical]] this is the partition-coexistent decentralised-substrate falsifier candidate, and it survives the test — strongly. Cephalopod cognition spatially partitions across (a) 8 arm-ganglia (b) central brain (c) optic lobes (d) stellate ganglion + chromatophore network (e) sucker ganglia (f) nerve ring. Each partition runs its local cascade slice: per-arm {L_arm ∘ I_segment ∘ C_local_sensorimotor}; ring I_ring composes them; central L_central + M binds. Unified behavioural output: C(M(...)). Decentralisation does NOT falsify substrate-identity; it provides the most explicit available anatomical evidence for spatial partition-coexistence as a realised pattern.
